subject: Agriculture
title: Food Miles Myth
description: A fast breakdown of Food Miles Myth for builders.

hook.text: Eating local sounds green. But a tomato shipped from Spain may have a smaller carbon footprint than one grown in a UK greenhouse.

buildup.text: Food miles measure distance, not emissions. Growing food matters more than moving it.

discovery.text: A ship carrying 10,000 tons of grain emits less CO₂ per kilogram-mile than a car carrying groceries from the store.

twist.text: Lamb from New Zealand shipped to the UK has a lower footprint than UK-raised lamb because NZ grass-feeds year-round.

climax.text: What you eat—especially beef vs. plants—dwarfs where it comes from in environmental impact.

punchline.text: Eat less meat to help the planet. Eat local for other reasons—but not carbon.

quiz.question: Why can food shipped long distances sometimes have a lower carbon footprint?
options: Production methods matter more than transport, which is only 6% of food emissions

details.summary: The food miles concept argues that food transported shorter distances is more sustainable. This topic challenges that assumption by examining how transportation is often a small fraction of a food's total environmental footprint compared to production methods.
details.whyItMatters: Buying local feels virtuous but may not reduce emissions if local production methods are less efficient. Understanding the full carbon footprint of food prevents well-meaning but ineffective consumer choices.
takeaways: Transportation typically accounts for less than 10% of food's total carbon footprint
How food is produced matters far more than how far it travels
Ship transport is extraordinarily efficient—thousands of times more so than air freight

faq.question: Why is the food miles concept considered misleading?
faq.answer: Transport accounts for a small share of most foods' total emissions. A tomato grown in a heated greenhouse locally can have a larger footprint than one shipped by sea from a sunny climate where it grew without artificial energy.

faq.question: When do food miles actually matter for sustainability?
faq.answer: Food miles matter most for air-freighted perishables like overnight berries or fresh fish. Sea and rail transport is so efficient that distance alone rarely determines environmental impact. Production methods dominate the carbon equation.
